Subject: Quick check — capacity ask for late-stage POC (Aurora)

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the call this morning. We pushed the internal stakeholders to prioritize Redwood for the POC and we're rapidly moving toward a commercial decision in the next 3–4 weeks. Before we lock terms with Procurement, a couple of asks from our infra team: can Redwood confirm ability to reserve ~12 x 80GB GPUs for a two-week ramp starting mid-May, with an option to scale to 24 if initial perf targets are met? We also need a short note on whether the capacity can be pinned to us-west-2 and whether you'd support a short (7–14d) soft-hold window prior to activation.

If you can send a short note back with availability and next steps (and any docs we should loop into Procurement), that'll help move the contract review along.

Appreciate it,
Ari

Questions for Ops (Ben/Monica):
- Do we have the physical capacity in US-W1 (us-west-2) for 12 dedicated 80GB-class GPUs between 2028-05-15 and 2028-05-31?
- Can we provide a 7–14 day soft-hold on those nodes (meaning they’re reserved but not charged until activation) and what language should we include in the MAP?
- If only partial capacity is available, what’s the recommended fallback (mix of 48GB/80GB, async region fallback to us-west-1)?

Aditya — will need a short note on sizing assumptions (model memory, concurrent sessions) so Sales/Procurement can show cost/throughput tradeoffs.

I’m copying Ari for transparency; aim to reply to them within 48 hours.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park

Kimberly / team — snapshot below based on current fleet plan and scheduled maintenance windows. Attaching the availability snapshot (availability_snapshot_q2.pdf).

Short answer: we can cover the 12x 80GB request in us-west-2 for the requested window as a soft-hold, with one caveat — we have one maintenance block on 2028-05-18 where ~4 nodes will be unavailable for 6 hours. We can either:
1) Shift the guaranteed activation window so the critical ramp avoids 2028-05-18 morning (preferred), or
2) Provide a mixed allocation: 8x 80GB + 4x 48GB (A40-class) to keep the ramp intact but with slightly reduced per-token throughput.

Operational notes:
- Soft-hold policy: we can mark a ‘soft-reservation’ for up to 14 days; billing starts only on activation or at the end of the hold window if activated by default per MAP. We’ll include a clause that allows a single one-time extension of up to 7 days with written notice.
- Pinning: we can pin to us-west-2 but recommend a clause that allows temporary routing to us-west-1 if forced capacity remediation is required; fallback would only be used with 6–12 hour notice and customer sign-off for region change.

Attachments: availability_snapshot_q2.pdf (capacity by zone), aurora_model_profile.csv (template for model footprint), mutual_action_plan_v4.docx (MAP draft).

Ben
Ben Carter
Capacity Operations Lead
Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Quick check — capacity ask for late-stage POC (Aurora)

Quick sizing notes for Aurora’s infra team to paste into Procurement/Eng notes:
- Assumptions: model peak memory 36–42GB, typical sequence length 1k tokens, avg batch size 4, target p99 latency 220ms.
- For these targets we recommend 80GB-class instances (A100-80GB or equivalent). 12 x 80GB will comfortably sustain ~350 concurrent sessions depending on request patterns; 48GB nodes can be used for lower-concurrency shards or batching-heavy workloads.
- If Aurora is open to quantized 4-bit runtimes with small accuracy delta, they could achieve similar throughput on 48GB nodes (not identical latency profile).
- Network/storage: recommend pre-warming model cache on the reserved nodes 48–72 hours prior to activation; this increases activation reliability for the POC.

I’ll add a short bullet list we can paste into the MAP describing: recommended node type, expected concurrent sessions per node, and pre-warm steps.

– Aditya
Senior Inference Engineer
Redwood Inference

Ari — thanks for the ask and the context. Summary and next steps below so Procurement has everything to proceed: 

Summary of availability (Redwood -> AuroraTech):
- Soft-reservation: 12 x 80GB-class GPUs in us-west-2 available for a 14-day soft-hold starting 2028-05-13, with activation window through 2028-05-27. Billing will begin on activation or at end of soft-hold if automatically activated per MAP.
- Maintenance caveat: a scheduled maintenance on 2028-05-18 will affect up to 4 nodes for ~6 hours. We recommend scheduling the heavy ramp outside that 6-hour period. If you require no maintenance during the ramp, we can provide a mixed allocation (8x80GB + 4x48GB) as an alternate.
- Pinning & fallback: we will pin capacity to us-west-2 but MAP will include a fallback clause that permits temporary routing to us-west-1 with 6–12 hour notice and customer approval.

Operational items we’ll include in the MAP and the activation checklist:
- Node types and expected concurrent sessions per node (Aditya to supply the short bullets).
- Pre-warm window: 48–72 hours recommended to pre-load model artifacts on pinned nodes.
- Soft-hold extension: one-time extension up to 7 days with written notice.
- Escalation contacts: Ben Carter (Capacity Ops) and Monica Patel (Customer Success).

Attachments: we’ve attached the availability snapshot and a draft MAP. I’ll also push a HubSpot deal update and the DocuSign MAP link to your contracts inbox.

Next actions for Aurora:
1) Confirm whether you want the straight 12x80GB allocation or the mixed allocation (8x80GB + 4x48GB) if you want to avoid the maintenance window.
2) If straight 12x80GB, confirm acceptance of the one-time extension clause and the pre-warm recommendation.
3) If Procurement is ready, we’ll route the MAP to DocuSign after you confirm the allocation choice.

I’ll mark this as high priority on our side and aim to move the MAP to DocuSign once you reply.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive — Strategic Deals
Redwood Inference
